record.paper_title: Padua points and “fake” nodes for polynomial approximation: old, new and open problems
record.original_question: For Padua and Padua-like point sets in [-1,1]^2, can one prove that the associated Vandermonde determinant has variables that separate and that the Vandermonde determinants for each coordinate direction satisfy the resulting commutative property?

evidence.quote: The Vandermonde determinant associated to the Padua and Padua-like points has variables that separate.
The claim in [11, Lemma 1] had a "gap". After some years, the Lemma was completely proved [42].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n\ge 1$ be an integer and let $\mathrm{Pad}_n\subset[-1,1]^2$ denote the set of Padua points of degree $n$, defined as the self-intersections and boundary contacts of the generating curve $\gamma_n(t)=(\cos(nt),\cos((n+1)t))$, $t\in[0,\pi]$. More generally, consider "Padua-like" point sets obtained from analogous Lissajous-type constructions in $[-1,1]^2$. Order the bivariate monomial basis $\{x^i y^j : 0\le i+j\le n\}$ in a fixed grading and form the Vandermonde matrix $V_n$ whose rows are indexed by the points of $\mathrm{Pad}_n$ and whose columns by these monomials.

Prove that the Vandermonde determinant $\det V_n$ factorizes as
$$\det V_n \;=\; C_n \cdot D_x(x_1,\dots,x_N)\cdot D_y(y_1,\dots,y_N),$$
where $C_n$ is an explicit constant, $D_x$ depends only on the $x$-coordinates of the nodes, and $D_y$ depends only on the $y$-coordinates, and that $D_x, D_y$ are themselves expressible as products of univariate Vandermonde determinants in the respective coordinates (the "variables separate" property), together with the corresponding commutativity of the factorization.
artifact.category_tag: Padua points and bivariate Vandermonde determinants
artifact.status_search_result: The variables-separating factorization of the Vandermonde determinant for Padua and Padua-like points was originally conjectured by Bos, De Marchi, and Waldron, with a gap in the initial lemma. The complete proof was later given, notably via results on bivariate Vandermonde determinants on almost-square grids (De Marchi, Usevich and related work), establishing the conjectured factorization.

status_evidence.title: On the Vandermonde Determinant of Padua-like Points
status_evidence.snippet: Conjectured formula for the Vandermonde determinant for Padua-like points that factors as a product of an x-coordinate factor and a y-coordinate factor.
status_evidence.claim: Original conjecture stating the separation-of-variables factorization.

status_evidence.title: On certain multivariate Vandermonde determinants whose variables separate
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes factorized formulas for bivariate Vandermonde determinants on almost-square grids, crucial for proving the Padua-like conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: Provides the proof that closes the gap and establishes the separation property.

status_evidence.title: A few remarks on 'On certain Vandermonde determinants whose variables separate'
status_evidence.snippet: Follow-up clarifying and completing the proof of the variables-separation lemma for Padua-like Vandermonde determinants.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms the lemma is completely proved.
